'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Ma'rib Campaign]]
***[[Houthi movement|Houthi]] forces attack [[Ma'rib]], with [[ballistic missile]]s amidst an ongoing offensive to capture the city. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/gulf/2021/02/26/Houthis-target-Marib-residential-area-with-ballistic-missile (Al Arabiya English)]
*[[2021 Kaduna and Katsina attacks]]
**Gunmen kill 36 people, wound several others, and burn down houses when they attack two villages in [[Kaduna State|Kaduna]] and [[Katsina State]]s, [[Nigeria]]. Several attackers are also killed during an [[Airstrike|air operation]] by security forces. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/25/gunmen-kill-36-in-attacks-in-northern-nigeria (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Armenian coup d'état attempt]], [[2020−2021 Armenian protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of Armenia|Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] warns of an attempted [[Armenian Armed Forces|military]] [[coup]] against him after the [[Armenian Army|army]] demands that he and his [[government of Armenia|government]] resign. In response, Pashinyan dismisses the head of the general staff of the armed forces and calls on his supporters to rally in his support. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-armenia-politics-pm/armenian-pm-warns-of-coup-attempt-after-army-demands-his-resignation-idUSKBN2AP0WW (Reuters)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**At least 14 people are killed at a [[religion in the Central African Republic|religious]] site in [[Bambari]], [[Central African Republic]], amid clashes between armed groups and security forces. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/25/at-least-14-killed-at-religious-site-in-car-amnesty (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Nine [[Mali Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed and nine others are wounded during a long exchange of fire with armed groups in [[Bandiagara]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/26/several-soldiers-killed-in-central-mali-attack (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Pro-[[Tatmadaw|military]] counter-protesters attack anti-[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] protesters during a rally against the [[military junta]] in [[Yangon]]. Some counter-protesters were armed with knives and clubs, while others used slingshots and threw stones to attack their opponents. [https://www.voanews.com/east-asia-pacific/myanmar-military-junta-supporters-clash-anti-coup-demonstrators (Voice of America)]
*At [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]]'s direction, the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] launches [[airstrike]]s against [[Iran]]ian-backed [[militia]] group [[Kata'ib Hezbollah]]'s structures in [[Abu Kamal]], [[Syria]], killing 17 [[Popular Mobilization Forces]] militants. The airstrikes are described as retaliation for a [[2021 Erbil missile attacks|recent rocket strike]] in [[Erbil]], [[Iraq]], which left two people dead and 13 others wounded, including American military personnel. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/26/us-strikes-iranian-backed-military-infrastructure-in-syria (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Ituri conflict]]
**Seven civilians are killed by [[CODECO]] militiamen in Banyari Kilo sector, [[Djugu Territory]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.radiookapi.net/2021/02/25/actualite/securite/djugu-7-personnes-tuees-par-des-miliciens-de-codeco-banyari-kilo (Radio Okapi)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Fukushima earthquake]]
**A man in his 50s is confirmed to be the first fatality of the February 13 earthquake that struck near [[Fukushima, Fukushima|Fukushima]], Japan, after his body is found buried in his destroyed home. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/02/27bcd1c39fd5-1st-death-confirmed-in-feb-13-northeastern-japan-earthquake.html (Kyodo News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
****The [[Government of Croatia|government]] confirms that bars, cafés, and restaurants can reopen their outdoor terraces on March 1. [https://www.thedubrovniktimes.com/news/croatia/item/10981-cafe-bar-terraces-to-reopen-on-monday-across-croatia (''The Dubrovnik Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****[[Cyprus]] announces that it will allow high schools, gyms, and indoor sports facilities such as swimming pools to reopen on March 1 as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases continue to decrease. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210225-more-schools-gyms-to-open-as-cyprus-eases-lockdown (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****The [[Czech Republic]] reports their first cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in [[South Africa]] in a group of people who travelled to [[Zanzibar]]. [https://english.radio.cz/south-african-covid-mutation-confirmed-cr-8710445 (Radio Prague International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Finland]]
****[[Prime Minister of Finland|Prime Minister]] [[Sanna Marin]] announces "tier-two" [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions for the next three weeks, which includes the closure of bars and restaurants, expanded [[remote learning]], and a ban on gatherings of more than six people beginning March 8 due to the spread of the [[Lineage B.1.1.7]] variant. [https://yle.fi/uutiset/osasto/news/finland_announces_march_shutdown/11808835 (Yle)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] extends their nationwide lockdown restrictions until March 15 due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases and the spread of [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://hungarytoday.hu/coronavirus-hungary-restrictions-extended-march-15/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports its first case of the B.1.525 variant first detected in [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.independent.ie/news/first-irish-case-of-b1525-strain-of-covid-19-confirmed-as-r-number-increases-40132928.html (''Independent.ie'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain]]
****[[Bahrain]] becomes the first country to approve the single-dose [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for emergency use. It is also the fifth vaccine to be approved in the country. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1815821/middle-east (Arab News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****The [[National Medical Products Administration]] grants conditional approval for a single-dose [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] made by [[CanSino Biologics]] and a vaccine made by [[Sinopharm]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/china-approves-covid-19-vaccines-wider-76108095 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] receives 500,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine from [[India]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/sri-lanka-receives-500000-doses-of-covid-19-vaccines-from-india/article33933291.ece (''The Hindu'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****[[Syria]]'s health ministry confirms that the [[Government of Syria|government]] has received COVID-19 vaccines from an unnamed "friendly country", adding that [[healthcare workers]] will be the first to be vaccinated beginning next week. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-health-moscow-coronavirus-pandemic-damascus-361874c0d82e09d92486bd242de4b661 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
***[[Algeria]] reports their first two cases of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant in a healthcare worker from [[Algiers]] and a person who traveled to [[France]]. [https://cn.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-algeria/algeria-detects-first-two-cases-of-uk-coronavirus-variant-idUSL1N2KV3HM (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] receives the first shipment of 904,000 doses of [[Sinopharm]]'s [[BBIBP-CorV]] vaccine. [https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/amp/argentina/shipment-of-900000-sinopharm-vaccine-doses-arrives-in-argentina.phtml (''Buenos Aires Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belize]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
***[[Belize]] reports their first case of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant in a member of the British Army Training Support Unit Belize who has been infected with this variant. [https://www.breakingbelizenews.com/2021/02/25/first-belize-case-of-uk-variant-of-covid-19-found-in-a-member-of-batsub/ (Breaking Belize News)]
*[[2020–21 H5N8 outbreak]]
**[[Afghanistan]] reports an outbreak of highly pathogenic [[H5N8]] [[bird flu]] on a [[poultry farm]] in [[Herat Province]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/afghanistan-reports-h5n8-bird-flu-on-farm-oie-101614254187360.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Western Cape]] reports their first case of [[African Swine Fever]] at two small farms in [[Mfuleni]], [[Eerste River]] in [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.news24.com/amp/news24/southafrica/news/ban-on-pig-sales-in-western-cape-as-african-swine-fever-detected-at-two-cape-town-farms-20210225 (News24)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[India–Pakistan relations]]
**[[India]] and [[Pakistan]] issue a joint statement indicating that both sides agree to [[Ceasefire|stop firing]] at each other at the disputed [[Line of Control]] border in [[Kashmir]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/india-pakistan-agree-to-stop-firing-at-kashmir-border/a-56683894 (DW)]
*[[Uyghur genocide]], [[China–Netherlands relations]]
**The [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|House of Representatives]] votes to recognize the [[Government of China|Chinese government]]'s treatment of its [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]] [[Islam in China|Muslim]] minority as [[genocide]], becoming the first [[European Union]] country to do so. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-netherlands-china-uighurs/dutch-parliament-chinas-treatment-of-uighurs-is-genocide-idUSKBN2AP2CI (Reuters)]
*The governing body of the [[International Civil Aviation Organization]] appoints Juan Carlos Salazar of [[Colombia]] as the new Secretary-General of the Organization succeeding [[Fang Liu]] of [[China]]. [https://www.icao.int/Newsroom/Pages/Juan-Carlos-Salazar-of-Colombia-appointed-new-Secretary-General-of-ICAO-.aspx (ICAO)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBTQ rights in Malaysia]], [[judiciary of Malaysia]]
**The [[Federal Court of Malaysia|Federal Court]], in a landmark decision, unanimously declares that [[Selangor]]'s [[sharia law]] provision on "[[sodomy|unnatural sex]]" is invalid and unconstitutional, as such offences fall under the jurisdiction of [[Law of Malaysia|federal law]]. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/02/25/federal-court-unanimously-declares-selangor-shariah-law-criminalising-unnat/1952701 (''Malay Mail'')] [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysian-wins-challenge-islamic-law-banning-gay-sex-selangor-14279784 (CNA)]
*[[Tax returns of Donald Trump]]
**Former [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s tax returns are given to [[New York County District Attorney]] [[Cyrus Vance Jr.]] [https://abcnews.go.com/US/trumps-tax-returns-manhattan-prosecutors/story?id=76110229 (ABC News)]
*[[USA Gymnastics sex abuse scandal]]
**Former [[USA Gymnastics]] coach [[John Geddert]] dies from [[suicide]] by a self-inflicted gunshot wound off [[Interstate 96]] in [[Michigan]], shortly after being charged with [[human trafficking]] and sexual assault of a minor. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-56205049 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Croix-des-Bouquets jailbreak]]
**Notable gang leader Arnel Joseph and other detainees escape from prison in [[Croix-des-Bouquets]], [[Haiti]], during a riot that also resulted in the death of eight people inside the jail, including the prison's director. Casualties are also reported in the city's streets. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/26/several-dead-as-gang-leader-escapes-in-haiti-prison-break (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[LGBTQ rights in the United States]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes to pass the [[Equality Act (United States)|Equality Act]]. The bill will now head to the [[United States Senate|Senate]] for a vote. [https://www.nbcnews.com/feature/nbc-out/house-representatives-passes-sweeping-lgbtq-rights-bill-n1258900 (NBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Facebook]] bans all accounts related to [[Myanmar]]'s military, the [[Tatmadaw]], as well as ads from military-controlled companies following the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|military coup]] against [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] and the military seizure of power on February 1. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/facebook-bans-myanmar-military-linked-accounts-coup/ (CBS News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]]
**Despite losing the last match 2–1 to [[São Paulo Futebol Clube|São Paulo]], [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] wins their seventh [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brasileirão]] and eighth national championship overall. [https://www.uol.com.br/esporte/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2021/02/25/sao-paulo-x-flamengo---brasileirao-serie-a-2020.amp.htm (UOL)]
